fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Add margin to the picker
fresh.background: One of the complaints we got about the picker styling for `<select>` was the double-border effect of the drop-down being placed immediately adjacent to the button. Because jamming the picker right up against the button looks awkward, we propose a margin (which is a commonly used effect) of 4px. This also addresses the concern @jakearchibald raised in https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1417

fresh.background: The icons we use for ::checkmark and ::picker-icon are not particularly useful to read aloud. The status of the control is already exposed to AT independently, so we propose using empty alt text for these glyphs:

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] select picker-icon glyph
fresh.background: The UA stylesheet for `<select>` currently uses `disclosure-open` for the `::picker-icon`. However this kind of large filled triangle tends to be too bold and pointy in comparison to the adjacent text, which has led many design systems, including the demo styles from last week's `<select>` styling discussion, to adopt a chevron design.

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Handle prefers-contrast and forced-colors by default
fresh.background: Although any color styling that the author sets will override all our rules, including those in a media query, we might want to make sure that if the author doesn't set anything, users get appropriate contrast.

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Vertically centering form control content
fresh.background: The UA stylesheet currently applies block-axis centering in a few places: options, radio buttons, checkboxes, and [buttons](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14190). But actually, when an input or select is sized larger than the text and icons it contains, its contents should also be centered.

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Vertically centering form controls that don't contain text
fresh.background: The text-containing form controls (text inputs, select, button, etc.) use baseline alignment in reference to their text contents. However checkbox, radio button, and range controls do not contain text. So currently, they sit on the baseline. This looks fine if they happen to be sized to match the text, but that's not always the case.

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Refine internal spacing in appearance: base controls
fresh.background: The default padding for `<select>`’s base appearance right now a) doesn’t adhere to good optical alignment due to the ::picker-icon and b) doesn’t provide enough spacing within the interactive elements (like option).

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Inherit currentColor into ::picker()
fresh.background: We decided to set the ::picker() colors to `CanvasText` on `Canvas` because we needed to ensure an opaque background for the overlay, but actually, we can probably do better here in matching the author's colors.

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Apply ::field-text/::field-content to select button contents
fresh.background: This is a follow-up from https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14255. The `<select>` element has two possible markup patterns. "Customizable select" adds an extra `button` and optional `selectedcontent` element to represent the duplicated `option` content and allow it to be styled independently. But traditional markup doesn't have these elements, it just contains `option`s.

fresh.title: [css-forms-1] Apply border-radius to all base appearance controls
fresh.background: A survey of design systems shows that a vast majority round the corners of their input controls to make them not-sharp: usually by 4px, sometimes by 6px. We propose adopting this general consensus by adding `border-radius: 4px` to the base appearance for `input`, `textarea`, `select` and `::picker`.
